speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Back in July this year, I uploaded a social media post that congratulated Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong for receiving an honorary fellowship from the Economic Society of Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The honour was the highest that the society, of which I am a council member, can grant.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: In my post I observed how I differed philosophically from Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: These have to do with differing beliefs about the philosophy of public policy, especially as it concerns market efficiency and fair distribution.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I used an example he raised in his dialogue, about the certificate of entitlement (COE) system and explained how, by relegating allocation decisions to an impersonal market, he implicitly accepted that such resulting allocations were fair, or as fair as they could potentially be.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I noted that there could be a difference between COE allocations based on market prices, versus individual needs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Singapore is a dense, urban city, and like all such cities, public transportation is rightly the cornerstone of intra-city commuting.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The Ministry of Transport (MOT) efforts should, rightly, be focused on expanding efficient, affordable and accessible public transport.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This includes addressing our over-congestion issues along certain Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) and Light Rail Transit (LRT) lines, including in Sengkang, the constituency that I represent and as discussed earlier today, and improving cross-island connectivity to reduce commute times, not downplaying the importance of the bus system as a last-mile solution given our hot and humid climate and ageing population, and a road system that is more inclusive of greener travel options.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I first spoke about Singapore's vehicle quota system (VQS), and the associated COEs, in a Workers' Party Motion filed in 2023, on the cost-of-living crisis.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: My speech at the time was focused on refining the system, as I understood it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Among the most important suggestions I offered was a supply-side change, to smooth the annual quota supply across a 10-year cycle, so that what is on offer every month would roughly be the same, and a demand-side one, to shift private hire car (PHC) bids to the Open Category (Cat) E.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: While it has been implemented with less vigor than I would have personally preferred, in the debate at the time, then-Transport Minister Chee explained that the Government's position was based on the desire to minimise disamenities that would result from introducing too many cars on the road in the short-term.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I am also hopeful that the Government will eventually come round to moving PHCs into the quota for Cat E, as it already does with taxis, so that their commercially-minded bids do not inadvertently distort demand for non-commercial use.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: In my speech, I also underscored how the VQS system resulted in our ability to enjoy uncongested streets, especially compared to other global cities, such as London or New York, which has, perhaps revealingly, since gone ahead with a road pricing scheme of their own.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: It would not be a mischaracterisation to state that I believe that the benefits of the system outweigh the costs and I do not favour its complete repeal.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Still, in my speech then, I also alluded to how, while the Government contends that private car ownership is a luxury rather than a need, there are certain groups for whom access to a car is much closer to a need than a luxury.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Today, I will build on that speech I delivered two years ago.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I hope to propose another refinement, this time not to improve its efficiency per se, but its equity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: To set the stage, I will first share my view on why certain groups are in greater need for private transport.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I will then discuss how the COE system can be further refined to account for not just ability to pay but also access according to needs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Any parent of a young child, of whom I am one, will grasp how game-changing it is to be able to directly ferry their kids from, say, one supplementary or tuition class to another, especially if their interests and talents differ, and instructors and schools are located all over the island.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Those who have potentially given up their own careers to take care of a parent battling perhaps cancer will appreciate the flexibility that private transport affords as they bring their father or mother to their chemotherapy sessions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: And it is a given that those who lack physical mobility due to a disability would benefit enormously from the independence afforded by a car.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Importantly, such groups are not unfamiliar to us.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: We have agencies, the Agency for Integrated Care and SG Enable, to coordinate elderly and disabled care, and an entire Ministry, the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF), whose raison d'être is to support families.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: We already have clear definitions for what constitutes a primary caregiver to seniors, who is a parent or guardian of a child as stipulated in the Young Persons Act and an MSF-accepted basis for those who are considered disabled in our social policies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: What else is common among these groups, however, is that their need for private transportation is more acute than that of the average citizen.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: They would, accordingly, benefit from financial support that would make a car more accessible to them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: One may argue that this lack of discrimination, if you will, is by design.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Rather than provide targeted support toward car ownership, the Government currently provides generalised financial assistance, which can easily be applied toward offsetting the cost of a COE.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Money is fungible and such generality allows each beneficiary household to decide for themselves whether the cash is better spent on transport, or any other need.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But yet, this Government has not, historically, shied away from choosing targeted support, so long as it felt that there could be potential spillover benefits from directing individual or corporate conduct.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: That is why our Community Development Council vouchers are targeted, because we wish to not only encourage household consumption via such transfers, but to also direct spending toward supporting our heartland businesses.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: That is why we grant businesses tax write-offs for qualifying research and development expenditures, so that they devote more resources toward growth-enhancing innovation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: That is why Ministry of Education directs its financial assistance scheme for low-income households toward educational expenses, such as fees and books, to help educate the next generation and, hopefully, break free from that cycle of poverty.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: By the same token, targeted support for car ownership can promote positive behaviours, such as children engaging in caregiving for their elderly father or mother, or time-strapped parents deciding to have their second or third child, or those with disabilities feeling sufficiently empowered to enter the workforce.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Such targeted mechanisms can serve as a signal of the values we place, as a society, on cultural norms, such as filial piety, family bonding, and care for the weak and downtrodden.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: One may say that it is hard to adjudicate between different groups with needs and so it is better not to do so at all, by leaving it to the market.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Or, you may say, like me, that we should not let the perfect be the enemy of the good and seek a way to help certain groups that we have already identified as more needy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This is not the first time that this House will have debated the merits of enabling greater access to COE for certain groups.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: In the 14th Parliament, then-Non-Constituency Member of Parliament Hazel Poa mooted the idea of a COE credits allocation framework, where tradable credits replace the existing price-based system.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Certain groups, families with young children, the elderly, the disabled, and those who have served National Service, would receive slightly larger allocations, in recognition of their greater needs, or greater contributions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: To blunt the fiscal impact, she suggested a base fee, which is either determined by car engine capacity or as a share of the vehicle's open market value.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The proposal's intent is similar to what I will suggest today: to better level the playing field between the genuine needs of certain households for a private vehicle, versus their ability to pay for a COE.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: It bridges the gap between need and affordability.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: In that regard, the spirit of the idea is sound.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: However, Ms Hazel Poa's proposal relies on a non-price system for the initial allocation, before subsequently subjecting these credits to market exchange, which introduces additional wrinkles of complexity and opacity to an otherwise straightforward auction-based pricing system.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The Government’s response to the proposal raised similar concerns about how it is complicated and runs the risk of inefficient pricing.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But then-Senior Minister of State for Transport Amy Khor also trotted out an old trope, that having the Government dictate differential credit allocations would be excessively subjective.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Senior Minister Lee, in his address, had made a similar point, that the market was the most fair and efficient way.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: While I agree that the Vickrey auction, on which the COE is based, is indeed an efficient mechanism, let us not pretend that it is actually fair or neutral.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Allowing prices to be dictated by the market simply abstracts from need, by allowing money to adjudicate between competing demands.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Those with more money will automatically be able to bid more, to secure the limited resource.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: It is only fair if we believe that the distribution of income and wealth in society is also always fair.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I will propose what I believe is a cleaner approach toward incorporating the needs of certain groups, which, if I may remind this House, we have already accepted are worth supporting, within the existing price-based COE system.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: To be concrete, we may consider a variant of the following.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This is a full waiver, which is already in place, in the form of the Disabled Persons Scheme.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Hence, a family of two children aged four and seven would receive a 10% discount, while one with three children aged between two and 13 would receive a 20% discount.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: A family with a five- and 15-year-old would not receive any discount, nor would single-child families.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The discount would apply at the time of purchase.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: COE prices would still follow market value thereafter.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Hence, should the vehicle subsequently be sold, the benefits would remain with the family that qualified for the discount in the first place.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: While some have speculated, based on the experience of the electric vehicle (EV) subsidy, that rebates might simply pass on into higher COE prices, this has not been definitively proven.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Perhaps more important, the much smaller segment of potential buyers which would qualify for such discounts makes it highly unlikely that they will materially move markets.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: To ensure that this system caters to genuine needs while keeping the system fiscally sound, we can accompany these with some form of means testing.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This is distance-based charging, which has already been foreshadowed by the roll-out of ERP 2.0.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Should COE prices fall alongside distance-based charges, it will certainly address some concerns by some of the groups that I mentioned.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But road pricing will bring its own set of fairness considerations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: After all, those living further away, such as estates in Punggol or Sengkang, will suddenly be subject to a higher distance charge just to get to work due to the unanticipated change in policy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This is a debate for another day, but I hope that the thoughts I offer today already hint at the importance of not just taking efficiency into consideration while evaluating who has the right to use our roads but that the equity considerations will come to the fore as well.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: COE policies have been debated extensively before in this very Chamber.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Many ideas have been proposed and debated over the years.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I want to take this opportunity to reiterate why we have this system and also to address some of the questions that other Members have raised during this week's Sittings on the COE.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: The COE system is neither perfect nor popular.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: But I am glad Assoc Prof Lim agrees that there is still a need for a COE system.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We do not have enough land for every person or even every household to own a car.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: If every household owns a car, we will have around 1.5 million private cars on our roads, which is more than two times the current car population.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: But today, 12% of our land is already occupied by roads.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Any additional land take by roads will come at the expense of other meritorious needs – housing, schools, hospitals, community facilities, things that are good for our people.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: This is why our approach is to focus on mass public transport, not car ownership.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I am very glad that Assoc Prof Lim agrees with me on this.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We let people make their own decisions on whether they want to spend their money on buying a car and therefore bid for a COE.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: With COE revenues, we can provide every Singaporean with high quality and affordable public transport.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: This way, we achieve the greatest good for the greatest number.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: This is the fairest approach because some people do not want to drive, some people are unable to drive and some people do not want to be burdened by a car loan.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: But everyone can use good public transport to get to where they want to go.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Assoc Prof Lim argues for a COE system based on needs and concepts of fairness.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Other Singaporeans have shared similar perspectives with me, suggesting groups who can be treated specially or be subsidised for car ownership.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I sympathise with many of these perspectives, in particular, families with young children or those sending elderly parents to medical appointments.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I know it is not easy navigating public transport with several young kids in tow or with a senior in a wheelchair, I understand that, even though it is much better now than, say, ten years ago, when the public transport system was not totally barrier-free.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I do not doubt that these families will benefit from a car.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: As an alternative, some of them use private hire cars or rent a car once in a while when they need it.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: These options are not perfect substitutes, but they come close and are more affordable than buying a car.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I have received many appeals for COE subsidies – or, as the Member proposed, discounts.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: But whenever we consider this, it is difficult to make the case, because rather than give one family a substantial COE subsidy, whether it is $10,000, $20,000, $30,000, we can redistribute the same amount of subsidy to benefit many more families, including those who do not want or who are not able to afford a car.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: For example, we can give many more families credits to be used for transport services as we have done with the Large Families Scheme or to defray other expenditures through cash or with vouchers.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: It is challenging for the Government to allocate COEs based on needs.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: What appears deserving to one person might not appear fair to another.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: For example, if we subsidise families with children – how many children?

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Or if we allocate based on income, we have to decide whether to do household income or personal income, or whether big households should be more deserving than small families.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Do we take away the car when the need is gone?

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: All these ideas sound very attractive, but no matter how one draws the line, there will always be people who fall on the wrong side of the line, who believe that they are more deserving.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: And we will still be here, at another Parliament Sitting, debating at this late hour, on how each line has been drawn.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I understand the concerns over the rising COE prices in recent months.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: But COE prices have continued to rise because of demand.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Electric vehicles, especially those from China, are being brought into Singapore cheaply.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: This means more money being put into COE bids.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Some people have suggested that PHC companies are responsible for driving up COE prices.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Less than 10% of bids have been won by car leasing companies this year.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Even if we remove all of the PHC bids, the price of the marginal bidders below the clearing price would not be much lower.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Should we have a separate COE category for PHCs or do we move them to Cat E as the Member suggested?

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Well, a separate category means we have to take quota away from Cat A and Cat B.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Would it be more than 10% or less than 10%?

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: If more than 10%, there would be fewer COEs for Cat A and Cat B than today.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: If less than 10%, there will be fewer PHCs to meet customer demand.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: And what would happen is there would be higher PHC fares and higher rentals for drivers.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: This will disadvantage Singaporeans who cannot afford a car and who can only rely on PHCs to get around.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Ultimately, we all want to do better for Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I share the same broader goal as Assoc Prof Lim of expanding connectivity for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Where we differ is in how to achieve that.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: For this Government, we make sure that we deliver the greatest good for the greatest number.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We do so by investing heavily in our public transport system.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We build new train lines that serve millions of journeys each day.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We build covered linkways, upgrade our footpaths and expand our cycling paths to make first- and last-mile journeys of public transport commuters more convenient and comfortable.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: The COE system should therefore be seen in this broader context.
